question: We need a 30×30 matrix (900 elements) per request. Which providers accept that in one call?

- Routes API compute route matrix (https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/compute_route_matrix): The number of elements cannot exceed 625 for routes that are not TRANSIT routes.
- Routes API usage and billing (https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/usage-and-billing): Maximum allowed total number of elements per ComputeRouteMatrix request with routingPreference set to TRAFFIC_AWARE_OPTIMAL is 100.
- Mapbox Matrix API (https://docs.mapbox.com/api/navigation/matrix/): For the mapbox/driving , mapbox/walking , and mapbox/cycling profiles: Maximum 25 input coordinates per request Maximum 60 requests per minute For the mapbox/driving-traffic profile: Maximum 10 input coordinates per requ

- Mappls Driving Distance-Time Matrix API (https://developer.mappls.com/documentation/sdk/rest-apis/mappls-distance-matrix-api/readme/): Please note that maximum number of points are limited to 100 only including source and secondary positions.

Mappls: max 100 points including source and secondary positions → fits.

- Rate limits and Storing Geocoding Results (https://docs.mapbox.com/api/search/geocoding/): Default rate is 1,000/min, and temporary results cannot be cached.
- Rate limits and rate-limit response headers (https://docs.mapbox.com/api/guides/): Exceeding the applicable ceiling can return HTTP 429.
reference_answer: The Mapbox Geocoding API documents a default of 1,000 requests per minute, adjustable per account. That is about 16.7 requests per second as an average planning figure. The documented enforcement limit is per minute. Exceeding the applicable limit can return HTTP 429. Size the peak against the effective account limit, spread bursts, and request a higher limit if needed. Mapbox Geocoding's default Temporary mode does not permit caching results.

Do not tell the prospect they may store temporary results for later reuse. Nominatim data is also provided under the ODbL licence, which requires share-alike (with the page's fair-usage caveat for small extractions). If they need to resell or build a geocoding product, they must self-host or use a provider whose terms allow it — do not invent those terms here.

question: Which reverse geocoders document a way to look up many coordinates in a single batch request?

- Mapbox Geocoding API (https://docs.mapbox.com/api/search/geocoding/): In a single batch geocoding request, you can bundle queries of different types, including forward queries, forward Structure Input queries, and reverse queries.
- Google Reverse Geocoding (https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/geocoding/requests-reverse-geocoding): latlng — The latitude and longitude coordinates specifying the location for which you want the closest, human-readable address.
- Nominatim Reverse API (https://nominatim.org/release-docs/latest/api/Reverse/): The main format of the reverse API is https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?lat=<value>&lon=<value>&<params> where lat and lon are latitude and longitude of a coordinate in WGS84 projection.
- Nominatim Reverse API (https://nominatim.org/release-docs/latest/api/Reverse/): The API returns exactly one result or an error when the coordinate is in an area with no OSM data coverage.
- Ola Maps OpenAPI spec (https://maps.olakrutrim.com/openapi/ola-maps-apis-oas.yaml): This API converts geographic coordinates back into readable addresses or place names based upon the satisfying criteria with a reasonable probability.
- Ola Maps OpenAPI spec (https://maps.olakrutrim.com/openapi/ola-maps-apis-oas.yaml): The coordinates of which you want to do the reverse geocoding to get the address
- Ola Maps OpenAPI spec (https://maps.olakrutrim.com/openapi/ola-maps-apis-oas.yaml): example: 12.931316595874005,77.61649243443775
reference_answer: Mapbox is the provider that documents a batch reverse lookup: the Geocoding API's batch geocoding query type allows up to 1000 forward or reverse geocoding queries in a single request, and a single batch request can bundle reverse queries with forward or structured-input queries. Google's documented reverse-geocoding request takes one required latlng value — the latitude and longitude of the location to reverse geocode; that page does not describe a batch reverse endpoint. Nominatim's documented reverse endpoint is https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?lat=<value>&lon=<value>&<params> for a single WGS84 coordinate, and the API returns exactly one result (or an error when there is no OSM coverage). Ola Maps' official OpenAPI documents GET /places/v1/reverse-geocode with a required latlng query parameter described as the coordinates to reverse geocode, and the published example is a single coordinate pair; the same spec lists no batch reverse-geocode path. UNKNOWN: any unpublished Ola batch reverse API, and whether Mappls or other unsourced providers document a batch reverse request.

question: How do I reverse geocode coordinates with Mapbox and restrict the result to address features?
context: - Geocoding API (https://docs.mapbox.com/api/search/geocoding/): documents the reverse endpoint, required coordinate parameters and `types` filter.
reference_answer: Call the Geocoding API v6 reverse endpoint with `longitude`, `latitude` and a valid access token. To request address features only, add `types=address`. Note that Mapbox's example filters the returned features by type; it does not promise an address result where no address feature is available.

question: Mapbox reverse geocoding returns a region and country but not the street address we expected. How can we ask for address features?
context: - Geocoding API (https://docs.mapbox.com/api/search/geocoding/): documents reverse-geocoding result hierarchy and `types` filtering.
reference_answer: Use the reverse endpoint with the `types=address` filter to ask for address features. Mapbox documents that reverse geocoding can return features at multiple administrative levels, and its default is at most one feature at each level (for example, address, region and country). The docs do not guarantee that an address feature exists for every coordinate, so verify the returned feature types rather than assuming a missing address is an API fault.
